summary: The reviewer wants the manual type check and r_stop_internal("Expected logical vector.") in r_lgl_which replaced with the standard r_stop_unexpected_type() to handle non-logical inputs.

The reviewer wants the styling changed so the standalone “else” followed by a separate “if” becomes a single “else if” on the same line for clarity in the block that may set effective_top_op to o->op_sibparent.

The reviewer wants you to avoid a dangling pointer by setting m->substitute to NULL after calling vine_file_delete(m->substitute), or otherwise not performing the delete here if a separate fix removes the need.
- Eliminate the warn(...) call that logs when bucketing_cursor_w_pos_delete is given a null pointer (i.e., remove the else warning and avoid emitting this warning).

The reviewer questions the hard compile-time error that forbids combining CYTHON_USE_MODULE_STATE with CYTHON_PEP489_MULTI_PHASE_INIT. They suggest this restriction is too strict because multi-phase init only allows, but doesn’t guarantee, multiple imports, implying the check should be relaxed rather than an unconditional error.

The reviewer requests moving the declarations of h and h_end into the for-loop initializer, i.e., declare and initialize both pointers within the for statement instead of a separate const declaration before the loop, for consistency with other code.

- The reviewer flags the new bare return inside the OPEN-state block (#if !H2O_USE_LIBUV).
- Concern: since defer_timeout is unlinked earlier, this early return might exit without scheduling any new timer (and the prior notify_write call was removed), leaving no timer linked.
- They want the logic adjusted/verified so we don’t return with the timer unlinked and no new timer or notifier set.

The reviewer questions the added condition “(len == 1 && path[0] == '/')” in the early return. They believe it’s redundant because later logic already fast-paths the “/” case by checking path[0] == '/' and skipping the loop. They suggest removing the added OR clause and relying on the existing optimization.

The reviewer wants the test to also handle client_protocol_version: either explicitly set it (in addition to actual_protocol_version) or assert it’s >= S2N_TLS13, to ensure the bug is actually covered.
The reviewer suggests not using LOG_TYPE_OTHER for stylist payments. They want a dedicated log type for stylist-related transactions in the pc->payzeny call.

- Add a missing flb_free(seq_index_str) before the goto error on the failure path after replace_uri_tokens.
- Change the null check from if (!tmp_key) to an explicit if (tmp_key == NULL).
- Move all variable declarations (e.g., tmp and name) to the top of update_retry_metric, before any statements, per the project's style guide.
- Replace all uses of flb_sds_cat with flb_sds_cat_safe in this function (for "--redacted--", kv->val, and "\n") so buffer realloc/address changes are handled safely.

The reviewer wants the Go proxy cleanup in flb_proxy_input_cb_exit to use the correct input-specific destroy routine (proxy_go_input_destroy) instead of proxy_go_output_destroy, since the latter doesn’t handle struct flb_plugin_input_proxy_context. They’re questioning the current call/removal and expecting proper cleanup of the input proxy context.
The reviewer requests freeing the existing core->prj->path before assigning prj_dir to it to prevent a memory leak when overwriting the field.
The reviewer wants null-handling added for newname to prevent a memory leak of newprjdir when newname is NULL (ensure proper cleanup or avoid allocation in that case).
The reviewer wants r_type_enum_free to handle a NULL input. Add a null check so the function can be called with a null member without dereferencing it (all free methods must accept null).

The reviewer wants a NULL check for value restored before using it. Specifically, guard the calls to PyException_GetTraceback(value) (and any dereference like Py_TYPE(value)) to avoid crashes when value can be NULL, as indicated by the previously present if (value != NULL && PyExceptionInstance_Check(value)) check.

- Do not build the _posixsubprocess extension on Windows platforms at all.
- Remove Windows-specific compatibility code (e.g., the MS_WINDOWS_GAMES dup/dup2 remapping).
- Restrict the module to POSIX targets only, aligning with existing POSIX platform checks.

The reviewer wants you to replace the manually constructed empty wait semaphore list (and the unused wait_value) with iree_hal_semaphore_list_empty() when passing the wait list to iree_hal_device_queue_execute.
Remove the redundant early return block after initializing dynamic symbols; rely on the subsequent iree_status_is_ok(status) check instead (no immediate release/return needed).

- The alignment check is incorrect: it currently checks data.data_length; it should validate alignment of the base buffer pointer instead.
- Adjust the error/reporting to reflect pointer alignment (not size).
- Acknowledge that wgpuBufferGetConstMappedRange may return unaligned pointers; in the short term, consider a flag to disable this check.
Remove the debug fprintf(stderr, "Looking up feature by key...") call from iree_cpu_has_required_target_features to prevent noisy output in tests/CI runs.
Switch the logger cleanup to use the pointer-based logger: call config->pLogger->clear instead of config->logger.clear, since some users may not populate config->logger.

- Change the loop index type to uint32_t so it matches count and avoids a type/sign mismatch in the i < count comparison.
- Verify whether -Wsign-compare (or -Wsign-compare-check) triggers a warning due to this mismatch, and report the exact line the compiler flags.

Reviewer questions the added cast to size_t in the loop condition (i < (size_t) count). They believe the sign-compare warning doesn’t apply here since both types are unsigned, so the cast seems unnecessary. If there is a valid reason to keep the cast, they want justification and consistent updates to similar loops elsewhere.
The reviewer questions the loop bound’s constant and cast, suggesting it should use (uint32_t) 0xFF instead of (size_t) 0xFFFFFF. They want the limit (and its type) adjusted accordingly.

Remove unnecessary (ssize_t) casts in the two EXPECT_EQUAL assertions:
- For s2n_client_hello_get_extensions_length vs client_extensions_len.
- For s2n_client_hello_get_extensions return value vs client_extensions_len.
Since both sides are already ssize_t, the casts aren’t needed.

- ASN1_STRING_length returns an int; don’t store it directly in a uint32_t.
- Keep the length variable signed (int), or explicitly validate it’s non-negative before any cast to an unsigned type.

The reviewer is concerned that casting r to int64_t while out->size is unsigned still results in an unsigned comparison, potentially masking issues and triggering/should trigger a sign-compare warning. They want the type mismatch in the comparison fixed so both sides use compatible signedness and the sign-compare warning is properly addressed.

The reviewer wants the fuzz tests to cover both configurations of kem_params.len_prefixed, not just the current true setting—i.e., provide versions/tests for len_prefixed = true and len_prefixed = false across all relevant fuzz tests.
- Expand the Kyber-specific test to run with both values of the len_prefixed flag (true and false), not just one, since the test is TLS-version agnostic.

- Make the comment explicit about draft versions: state that only draft 0 requires the length prefix, while drafts 1–5 do not.
- Clarify that this is why the code checks tls13_pq_hybrid_draft_revision == 0, instead of using vague “earlier/later drafts” wording.

- The config entry is mismatched: it uses the key/name and description for "use_ansi" but maps to the struct field ignore_missing_channels.
- Reviewer requests using the correct parameter name (e.g., ignore_missing_channels) and an accurate description that matches that behavior, removing the ANSI-related text.

The reviewer wants the deallocation of file_entries to use the standard free instead of flb_free, since the memory was allocated with malloc, and removing or using the Fluent Bit allocator could cause issues.
- Remove the early-return check for list->next == NULL in flb_ml_parser_destroy_all, as mk_list_init() should guarantee the list is initialized and makes this check unnecessary.

- Rename the config option key "buffer_rcv_size" to "receive_buffer_size".
- Update all references accordingly, including the struct member used in offsetof (struct flb_syslog, buffer_rcv_size) and any other occurrences.

The reviewer wants you to replace the manual FILETIME high/low to 64-bit conversion (int64_t ldap with UINT64(ft.dwHighDateTime, ft.dwLowDateTime)) in filetime_to_epoch with a ULARGE_INTEGER to hold the QWORD value.
The reviewer notes that the eprintf ("%x\n", stack_off); debug print will flood the console during analysis (e.g., running aaa) and should be removed or otherwise suppressed to avoid spamming output.

Replace the direct pj_new() call in r_core_diff_show_json with the core’s PJ creator (corepj.new via the available core instance) so user-configured options (indent, colors, 64-bit number formatting) are respected.
The reviewer wants to remove the “else if (id == -1)” that follows a branch which already returns (after return strdup(...)); avoid using else after return by de-nesting that block.
Remove the unnecessary else after a return in archinfo’s DATA_ALIGN case. If the CPU matches, return 1; otherwise rely on the existing return 2 after the if, avoiding else-after-return.

- Move the full-graph printing block (the if (fullGraph) loop) to the else branch of if (*match), so that when grepping (match is present) it doesn’t also print the full graph, avoiding duplicate output and ensuring grep behavior works as expected.
Use winsock2.h on Windows without conditional checks—remove the MS_WINDOWS_GAMES-based switch and stop including winsock.h.

The reviewer questions the necessity of the null-check on exc after PyErr_ExceptionMatches(PyExc_StopIteration) succeeds, implying PyErr_GetRaisedException() should not return NULL in that case and the defensive if (exc) can be removed/simplified.
- Remove the redundant comment “Check if the exception is indeed an AttributeError” before PyErr_GivenExceptionMatches, since the call is self-explanatory.
Reorder the preprocessor checks so the MS_WINDOWS_NON_DESKTOP/GetCurrentProcessId case comes before HAVE_GETPID, incorporating the related changes noted in other comments.

The reviewer flags unsafe reference handling: Py_DECREF(iterable) occurs while iterable is still on the stack, so on goto error the stack holds an object it no longer owns. They want the DECREF/ownership ordering adjusted so iterable isn’t decref’d while still on the stack before the error jump.

- In isfile(), check the return value of GetFileInformationByHandleEx before using FileBasicInfo/attributes.
- Only treat the handle as a filesystem entry (and then check not-directory) if this call succeeds.
- If the call fails, treat it as non-filesystem (e.g., device like "\\\\.\\C:") and thus not a file.

- The patch looks unfinished: the else-if chain after “cache-invalid” is broken (closing brace removed) and “transfer-address” is now called without its condition.
- The “worker-init” branch is still commented out.
- Reviewer asks whether you intended to finish these changes in this PR or defer them to a future one.
Remove the commented-out dead code (e.g., the // unlink_recursive(workspace); line) from workspace_delete instead of keeping it commented.

The reviewer wants the third argument in the itable_nextkey call to be a void** (pointer-to-pointer), not cast as (void*). Specifically, change the cast from (void*)&value to (void**)&value to match the expected signature and avoid compiler warnings.

The reviewer is asking to add explicit error handling for wait_for_shutdown. Since the underlying wait_for_event can return an error, they want this call either wrapped in GUARD_EXIT or for the code to clearly decide to continue despite the error, making the intended behavior on failure explicit.
Add an early null-check for the input parameter using RESULT_ENSURE_REF(conn) before dereferencing conn->handshake.io in s2n_handshake_transcript_update.
Add a null-pointer check for conn (ENSURE_REF(conn)) at the start of s2n_handshake_message_send before dereferencing conn->handshake.io.
The reviewer suggests replacing the second conditional (checking version < S2N_TLS13) with an else branch of the first if (version >= S2N_TLS13), since the conditions are complementary.

The reviewer wants the cipher suite list reordered to keep ECDSA variants before their RSA counterparts. Specifically, the AES_256_CBC_SHA pair is currently reversed (RSA listed before ECDSA); adjust to prefer ECDSA first for consistency and future dual-cert support.

- Expand the conflict condition to also check DEF_NONLOCAL (not just DEF_LOCAL | DEF_GLOBAL).
- Consider removing DEF_GLOBAL from the check, as it appears unreachable due to earlier handling when setting DEF_COMP_ITER; tests pass without it.
Remove the redundant non-negative check for data_len (RESULT_ENSURE_GTE(data_len, 0) and its comment) since the function already returns early when data_len < 0.
The reviewer wants the size check corrected: the comparison casts r to int64_t but expected_size is unsigned. Align the types or adjust the check to avoid a signed/unsigned mismatch.

The reviewer wants the condition to explicitly check for OCSP status requests. Instead of sending when status_request_type is anything except NONE, only send when status_request_type == S2N_STATUS_REQUEST_OCSP.

- Reviewer questions the necessity of the comments around s2n_recv_server_status_request, especially the “used in fuzz test” note.
- They suggest removing the fuzz-test reference since usage can be found via search.
- They caution against leaving a stale comment if the fuzz-test reference is removed, implying the comment should be cleaned up or removed to avoid misleading information.
Change the log level when no functions are found in r_core_diff_show_json: use an error-level log instead of info for the “No functions found, try running with -A or load a project” message.
Remove the redundant "Warning:" prefix from the R_LOG_WARN message in parse_type (keep the warning log, just drop the "Warning:" text).
The reviewer suggests changing the include guard from MS_WINDOWS_GAMES to MS_WINDOWS so <wincrypt.h> is included for all Windows builds, asking if there’s any downside to broadening the condition.

- Restore the decref of dcopy, but place it before the Done: label.
- Use Py_DECREF(dcopy) instead of Py_XDECREF(dcopy).

- Remove the custom wrapper function flb_sds_snprintf_realloc; it’s unnecessary.
- Use flb_sds_printf() for formatted appends since flb_sds_t auto-reallocates.
- Use flb_sds_len() to obtain the final length instead of manual size calculations.
Simplify the mutex unlock condition: remove the redundant thread-safety check and rely solely on locked (replace "u->thread_safe == FLB_TRUE && locked" with just "locked").
The reviewer wants all pointer null checks changed from shorthand (!ptr) to an explicit comparison (ptr == NULL), including this ctx check and similar occurrences elsewhere.

- Stop storing time_when_compatibility_checked under q->stats.
- Make it a direct field on q (suggested name: q->last_time_tasks_fit_check) since it isn’t a stat, and initialize/update it there.

- The code no longer populates the wlr_drm_format_set (dmabuf formats for RENDER/SAMPLED). The reviewer wants the logic that adds formats/modifiers to the format_set restored or ensured so the set isn’t left empty.
The reviewer wants the inline TODO comment block in the if(!infer_locals(...)) section removed before merging.
The reviewer suggests removing the local assert(base_index >= 0) in this function, since the same assertion will be enforced in parse_decode_context, making this check redundant.

- Limit the test to TLS 1.3 only; it shouldn’t cover TLS 1.2 fallback/self-downgrade behavior.
- Remove the conditional branch using s2n_is_tls_12_self_downgrade_required and the expected failure path.
- Apply the same restriction to the following test as well.

Move the s2n_is_tls13_fully_supported() check to the start of the test (around line 4) so the entire test only runs when TLS 1.3 is supported, since both success and failure cases require TLS 1.3 for early data.
Remove the spi_set_drvdata(spi, indio_dev) call because the stored drvdata isn’t used anywhere, so keeping it is unnecessary.
Change the for-loop index variable from size_t to ssize_t to match total_data_recv and avoid the cast.

- Simplify the API by removing the session_resumed parameter from print_connection_data.
- Have print_connection_data accept only s2n_connection* and internally retrieve whether the session was resumed (and any other needed data), avoiding duplicate/externally passed state.
The reviewer wants the comment corrected: replace “HelloRetry” with “Hello Request” (TLS 1.2), aligning with TLS_HELLO_REQUEST and the intended exception.

The reviewer questions the usefulness of the `max <= S2N_TLS13` check in the condition and wants the logic to rely only on the minimum version (i.e., focus on `min` when determining TLS 1.3 support), suggesting the `max` check be removed or justified.

The reviewer wants the function client_hello_noop_cb to have internal linkage and follow the project’s naming convention:
- Mark the function as static.
- Rename it to include the s2n_ prefix (e.g., s2n_client_hello_noop_cb).

The reviewer wants compression detection to use the chunk’s compression status flag (is_compressed) instead of checking compressed_chunk_id != 0, to ensure a single, consistent way of determining compression status throughout the code.
- Update the error message for the 'x' option to use "-x" (lowercase) instead of "-X" in "invalid server address specified for -X".
Reviewer suggests moving the two DCHECK_GE validations (num_live_tablets and leader_count) to execute before acquiring the lock, reducing the critical section.

The reviewer wants ZERO_TO_DISABLE_DEFER_CLEANUP(public_key) moved earlier—immediately before or right after assigning public_key to cert_chain->...->public_key—so that if s2n_cert_chain_and_key_set_names fails, cleanup behavior is correct and doesn’t risk double-free or misuse.
Change the memcpy length argument to use digest_length instead of data_len, so only digest_length bytes are copied and large buffers don’t cause undefined behavior.

The reviewer questions the hardcoded PSK_SECRET_SIZE_MAX (2048) limit, asking for justification of why a secret size cap is needed and whether this limit is exposed/advertised (e.g., part of a public interface).

The reviewer says the “#ifndef _MSC_VER” guard is redundant because if WIN32 isn’t defined, _MSC_VER won’t be either. They want the _MSC_VER check (and its block defining MAY_HAVE_FTRUNCATE and including <unistd.h>) removed or consolidated with the WIN32-based logic.

- Decide whether timestamping is platform-specific (Linux-only) or platform-agnostic.
- If Linux-only: guard all related pieces (listener_config_t::timestamping, the add_listener timestamping argument, and related code) with #if defined(__linux__), not just this assignment.
- If platform-agnostic: do not silently override the configured timestamping flag here based on platform; keep the flag consistent from config to usage.
Rename functions that contain "cert_get_cert" to drop the redundant second "cert". For example, change s2n_cert_get_cert_der to s2n_cert_get_der across all similar occurrences.
Change the struct so that ai_addr and intf_addr are direct sockaddr_storage members (not pointers), eliminating related dynamic allocation and cleanup logic.

The reviewer requests removing the H2O_CONFIGURATOR_FLAG_DEFERRED flag from the "strict-match" directive in h2o_configurator_define_command, since it doesn’t depend on other global/host-level directives and doesn’t need deferred merging.

The reviewer wants to remove the early return when the datagram flow is not found, so the function continues to dispose all other properties. In other words, handle the missing datagram flow without exiting early, maintaining consistent per-property cleanup (including the last property).

Simplify CompareByHost to always sort replicas by ts_desc->permanent_uuid, removing the logic that prefers http_addresses hostnames. Rationale: permanent_uuid is expected to be non-empty and provides sufficient, stable ordering.

The reviewer wants the precondition to verify the blob’s allocation state, not its current size. Replace the check on b->size with a check on b->allocated to ensure the blob hasn’t been previously allocated.
Use active_segment_->Size() (instead of written_offset()) when updating metrics_->wal_size after a successful close.
Remove the redundant zero-initialization of *psk. Since s2n_blob_zero(&mem) already zeroes the memory backing psk, the explicit "*psk = (struct s2n_offered_psk){ 0 }" line should be deleted.
Change the log_wal_size metric to use kilobytes (kBytes) as its unit instead of generic units.
The reviewer wants the loop to short-circuit: stop searching (e.g., break/return) as soon as a cipher suite match is found, instead of continuing to iterate through all suites.
Reviewer requests removing the unused fd_set wait_set and the associated FD_ZERO/FD_SET calls, since the code now relies on poll (pfd_read) and these are no longer needed.
The reviewer wants the inline _currentIndex++ removed from the AnimationFrame/GetICN call and incremented on its own line, avoiding combining multiple expressions in a single statement.

Remove the localized placeholder workflow for the lighthouse count ("%{count}" + StringReplace + _()) and instead use std::to_string(lighthouseCount) directly when creating the text for lighthouseControlledElement, since a pure number doesn’t need translation.
Replace the literal 0 argument with Dialog::ZERO in the calls to fheroes2::showKingdomIncome and fheroes2::showLighthouseInfo within Kingdom::openOverviewDialog.

The reviewer wants all leftover debug code removed from CheckWeightsFunctor—specifically the commented-out std::cout debug statements and any related temporary debug checks—so the code no longer contains these debug remnants.

The reviewer wants you to stop blindly dereferencing from.data_as_pattern()->options() when setting options.case_insensitive. Add a safety measure: either assert the pointer is non-null if it must exist, or check for null and handle missing options to avoid crashes with older patterns that lack this field.

- Replace the copy of fields_record into config_record["fields"] with a move (use std::move(fields_record)) to avoid an unnecessary copy.
- Do not change the loop to use std::move due to structured bindings friction and low performance impact.
Use move semantics when setting config.fields: assign parsed_extractors to config.fields at that spot using std::move to avoid copying.
Use move assignment instead of copy when assigning fields_record into config_record["fields"] to avoid unnecessary copying.
The reviewer requests replacing qsizetype with int for sBStart to maintain compatibility with Qt 5.9.5, which doesn’t provide qsizetype. The previous int type was acceptable.

- Simplify the emptiness check: remove redundant comparisons to "", using only power.isEmpty() || toughness.isEmpty().
- Reevaluate the surrounding logic: the next if already checks both values; the current if’s purpose appears incorrect or redundant.
- Prefer building the final power/toughness output by conditionally appending existing values and joining them with the separator, instead of the current conditional setup.
The reviewer requests a style change: declare the variable as "const auto" (instead of "auto const") and rename "savedChannels" to "saved_channels", updating its usages accordingly.

Reviewer asks to widen the notify condition: change the comparison from < to <= when checking sequence_number against last_sequence_number_sent_, so unsent_changes_cond_ is notified even when the removed change is exactly the last sent (ensuring wait_for_acknowledgement unblocks appropriately).

- Change the delete_contained_entities() call in step 3 to be invoked on the regular participant instead of statistics_participant.
- Rationale: aligns with typical user usage and avoids potential virtual dispatch issues.
- The block comment above plugin_set_config is incorrect (mentions plugin_write). Update the comment so it matches the actual method name and intent for plugin_set_config.

- Remove the getMux() accessor from P025_data_struct, since it’s only used once in a log statement.
- Use the actual setting directly in that log instead.
- Goal: reduce binary size by a few bytes.

- Instead of storing only the numeric ID in hoot:id, include the element type (Node/Way/Relation) with the ID (e.g., “Way(758208161)”), likely via getElementId().toString().
- Update the unit test to assert the expected hoot:id format (type plus numeric ID).

- The Debug::Time check here duplicates a prior check (line 12689), so this guard should always be true.
- As a result, the restore variable and the conditional clear/set of the "time" flag are unnecessary.
- Simplify by removing the redundant guard/restore logic around the debug time flag.

- Remove the redundant inner `if (fd)` inside the block guarded by `if (url.isEmpty() && (fd = findFileDef(...)))`.
- Call `copyFile(...)` directly within that block, since `fd` is already guaranteed non-null by the outer condition.
The reviewer wants the local variable declaration changed to a const pointer: replace “auto curr_{{FIELD_NAME}} = {{FIELD_NAME}}();” with “const auto* curr_{{FIELD_NAME}} = {{FIELD_NAME}}();”.
The reviewer wants the length check updated so it matches the 4-character substring. Change the condition from checking strlen(name) >= 3 to >= 4 before taking substr(0, 4).

- Make NaN detection case-insensitive (accept "nan", "NAN", etc., not just "NaN").
- Validate token boundaries after NaN: require an appropriate delimiter (e.g., whitespace) and avoid treating "NaN0.0m" as two values.
- Clarify how strict the parser should be about whitespace following NaN.

The reviewer wants concurrency() to return the max concurrency from the space instance (m_space_instance->m_maxConcurrency) instead of using the global singleton (Impl::SYCLInternal::singleton().m_maxConcurrency).

The reviewer questions the necessity of including MantidAPI/AlgorithmRuntimeProps.h and MantidAPI/IAlgorithm.h. Since only IConfiguredAlgorithm_sptr is used, they want these MantidAPI headers removed if they’re unused.
Add a validation in TimeSplitter constructor to ensure all values in X are non-negative (>= 0). If any value is negative, throw a RuntimeError, as specified by the docstring.
The reviewer wants the invalid_argument throw moved into a switch default case, instead of throwing after the switch, to handle unexpected ALFData values within the switch structure.

The reviewer questions the necessity of the if (workspace) check in the MatrixWorkspace overload, suggesting it may be a leftover from the optional<double> overload and should likely be removed (i.e., set the property without the null-check).
The reviewer requests placing the fallback MemStat definition in the non-profiling branch inside the amrex namespace (i.e., avoid defining it in the global namespace).
Reviewer requests correcting the z-direction flux array: change fzfab to reference fluxes[2] instead of fluxes[1].
Add handling for niu_max_ncpus_pct: if it’s 0.0 (meaning “no restriction”), set it to 100.0 before calling DisplayValue, consistent with max_ncpus_pct and cpu_usage_limit.

- Confirm whether this change should target the main branch.
- Justify the default assignment “= true” for the params_dict argument (why a boolean default for something named params_dict), or adjust accordingly.
Move the hero->SetSpellPoints(std::max(...)) call inside the if (hero != nullptr) block, placing it immediately after hero->PickupArtifact(...).

- The call that scouts using the current hero at the other hero’s position is wrong, as it applies the current hero’s scouting radius to the other hero’s location.
- Scouting should be performed by the other hero using their own scouting radius/statistics, not by the current hero on the other hero’s position.

- The reviewer finds the current input-validation logic brittle and wants it rethought.
- They want to avoid reading input inside conditional branches; input should be taken in a single place, not within if blocks.
- Consolidate/clean up the validation flow for the size range check (1–30) to remove duplicated std::cin calls.
The reviewer suggests using the parser “blank” instead of “space” for the optional whitespace (optional_ws) before the plugin name, likely to avoid consuming newlines and only allow spaces/tabs.

The reviewer wants indexers keyed by field offset (nested path) rather than a flat column index. They disagree with the TODO about indexing by column and prefer using offset (e.g., via qualified_record_field) to support indexing fields inside nested structures like records in lists.

The reviewer wants the SQL query construction in SaveTimers to use fmt::format instead of StringFormat (i.e., replace the StringFormat call that builds the REPLACE INTO bot_timers query with fmt-style formatting).
Replace the StringFormat-style '%u' placeholders in the fmt::format SQL string with fmt-style '{}' placeholders for bot_id, timer_id, and timer_value.
The reviewer points out that the args vector is unused—not passed to EventNPC—and it wasn’t used for NPCs before either, so removing it doesn’t change behavior.
Reorder the includes so that C++ standard library headers (e.g., <string>) appear before project headers (fastdds/*), following eProsima’s/Google’s include order guidelines.

The reviewer wants the mutex scope in get_listener_for narrowed so that the final return (calling subscriber_->get_listener_for(status)) occurs after releasing listener_mutex_. Only the access/check of listener_ should be within the lock; the fallback return should be outside the mutex.

The reviewer asks to clear the moved-from object’s callback count in the move constructor—i.e., set rValueResource.active_callbacks_ to 0 (similar to setting rValueResource.mValid = false) so the source doesn’t retain a stale callback count.

- Avoid emitting the same JSON key for all three GPIO entries; each pin should have a distinct label.
- Build the key dynamically (e.g., "TaskDeviceGPIO" + index) instead of hardcoding separate if blocks for 1/2/3.
- Add the appropriate string concatenation/include (e.g., StringConverter.h) if required to support building the key.
- Remove the commented-out enum handling line in SwiftGenerator’s default value logic (delete the dead/commented code).
The reviewer is questioning the unused counter variable i in init() (both its declaration and the i++ inside the loop) and wants it removed since it serves no purpose.

The reviewer questions why several legacy/threading-related lines are left commented out (thread_local note, WorkerThread pointer, SOFA_THREAD_SPECIFIC_PTR, and the DefaultTaskScheduler thread map). They want to know if these comments are intentionally kept or should be removed/cleaned up.
The reviewer suggests removing the commented-out dead code: the three-line for-loop that sets qm_virial[i] = 0.0.

The reviewer questions the use of an immediately-invoked lambda to compute mpi_local_size and wants this unusual one-off lambda pattern removed or replaced with a clearer, conventional initialization (and made consistent with the Threads implementation).

- The reviewer objects to removing setFaceDown(false) from Server_Card::resetState.
- This change causes a major info-leak: when a facedown card moves between battlefield and deck, its state is reset and then the facedown flag is checked; with the new behavior, opponents are incorrectly shown the card’s identity.
- They want facedown state handling during reset/move restored or kept consistent so moving a facedown card remains unknown-to-unknown and does not reveal the card to opponents.
